searchText: Update: Prysm has an issue on devnet3, its having trouble syncing past 2000 due to rate limiter is getting shared between block and blob. Peers will getting dropped after a while. I'll attemp to fix this today am getting invalid stateroot as soon as capella starts does this testnet includes bounded withdrawals? iirc withdrawal is treated as no-op are you passing the latest spec test? so disabled withdrawals? yes by disabling withdrawals in spec tests via some configuration thats why i asked this but from reply i inferred that withdrawals is enabled Prysm follows the spec here If people want withdrawal we can restart devnet with withdrawal enabled ok, let me disable withdrawals and try to sync, but it would be good that we now run with proper withdrawals yes am able to sync past capella now am getting stuck on slot 159, so not syncing slot 160 Maybe we can run withdrawals starting devnet4. Withdrawal also has alignment issues such as blockValue and bounded check. It will be good to wait for it to be more stable What is the error? ahh getting this error Ah forkDigest. <@159152274659082240> and I were talking about it I haven't had time. I'll look into it soon these are the forkdigest mappings we got: ```typescript { forkNameByForkDigest: Map(5) { '30dcb640' => 'phase0', '77fcecf8' => 'altair', '48f5acb3' => 'bellatrix', '47052036' => 'capella', '3715b697' => 'eip4844' }, ``` one other thing, the config.yaml in the config, can we restore PRESET_BASE to mainnet, CONFIG_NAME can stay testnet i guess also i guess now am being rate limited with all the random experiments i been trying 😅 Yeah prysm is being really strict, pushed a fix in the morning Need to update nodes cc <@159152274659082240> This matches what I have locally okk, so how would we be getting the `5cff0600` in req/res response 🤔 this is what I got from peer `16Uiu2HAm1oEch6uXffoGZ32kPTiyjycfX9yDuBJSWtmagBSk9HTN`. Not sure who that is ``` local 3715b697 remote 4a26c58b ``` I think we should set up a real bootnode so bad remote here as well i got this `5cff0600` from the first enr which was listed in the hackmd i think <@159152274659082240> / <@427491045308235776> i was trying to generate a tx test for minimal preset for lodestar using java script binding for c-kzg, but i discovered that FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB is hardcoded , would it be possible to have an "init" function which can set these values in the lib, else we should just make the minimal preset value for FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB same as mainnet I don't see your peer connection or request on the first enr node. Not sure where that fork digest comes from. Could you try using the other two enrs? I think i see the issue. A context isn't written in the response. <@363800010518822915> according to the code this is because `blobs_sidecar_by_range` uses the `v1` schema. Though I don't see this behavior explained in the spec. Shouldn't the fork digest always be included after atlair regardless of the schema version? So the invalid context you were seeing is probably the first 4 bytes of the `BlobsSidecar` message. Yea this also wasn't clear to me ^ I think we might as well include context bytes even though we don't technically need them so long as blobs exist in one fork we should probably include context bytes to future proof it .. I'm not sure if this necessitates this becoming a V2? or if we can just label it a V1 and be explicit it includes context bytes? yup let's do that. Leaving it as V1 with context. that way there would be no need for v2 😆 I don’t think you can make the minimal preset the same as Mainnet because the minimal one is used for performance purposes. I asked Dan a week or so ago about this and it would require you to rebuild the bindings because that constant is hardcoded at compile time So it’s possible to have a minimal npm package and a Mainnet npm package, but that’s quite messy imo yes it would be super messy, but apart from spec tests, it effectively undermines using the minimal so the compile time setting is not ideal. i think the better UX would be to specify the values on init/loading the lib, but i am not sure how much work it would be to make them dynamic Its a property of the c library, so its a bit of effort to config that at runtime. I can look into solutions and get back to you 🙂 In the meantime I guess you can use mainnet preset and its not a hard blocker? yes, its not a blocker and probably can figure out a way to overrdde it in my tests and thanks for looking into this 🙏 <asn_d6> we could make it a dynamic parameter the same way the trusted setup is loaded in runtime but we should have a strong reason for it. feature bloating the c lib is no bueno. (apart from the extra function we would also probably need to add a bunch of sanity checks to make sure that the specified parameter is reasonable) ^^^ agreed, then we should just do away with differences in minimal and mainnet settings I think they were there for a reason related to the consensus-specs being in python how are the other go/rust libs dealing with it? pawan is sick, but I think he's adding a compile time flag for the minimal and mainnet `FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB` config to the rust bindings https://github.com/ethereum/c-kzg-4844/pull/16
